title: qf.v1
description: The framework configuration of a product, qf.yaml: where the work products live and which skill fills each stage (slots). Human-owned and valid before the agent starts. Where plugins are installed is not here — it depends on the machine (environment.v1) — and plugin versions are not tracked: the gates prove the work product, whatever produced it. The product's tech stack is a work product of SWE.2 (stack.v1).

contract.description: The contract version this file is written against.

code_dir.description: Where the code and its tests are stored. The gates search it for @unit markers; every file with @unit[x] has x's component id as a segment of its path.

verification_plan_file.description: The verification plan (verification_plan.v1), one Markdown file with a fenced ```yaml verification_plan block.

env_variables_file.description: The environment variables the code reads (env_variable.v1), one Markdown file with a fenced ```yaml env_variable block per variable, written with the detailed design.

integration_tests_dir.description: Where the component and integration tests are stored (SWE.5), apart from code_dir so the unit gates never read them; the stack's integration suite runs them.

software_tests_dir.description: Where the software-level tests are stored (SWE.6), each naming the requirement it verifies with @sdoc; the stack's software suite runs the software-level ones, its e2e suite the system-level ones.

observability_dir.description: Where the alert, dashboard and health-check definitions are stored (principle #37-#39), each naming the observability requirement it serves with @sdoc.

framework_dir.description: Where the framework is checked out as a git submodule pinned to a released commit (SUP.1 BP1, BP2); the product's CI runs the gates from there.

ci_file.description: The product's CI workflow that runs the gates (e.g. .github/workflows/quality_gates.yml); a code owner must approve every change to it (SUP.1 BP1).

framework_feedback_file.description: The framework feedback log (principle #47): every framework weakness found while building, and every framework version bump accounted for.

releases_dir.description: Where the release records are stored (release.v1), one <version>.yaml per release, added by the release pull request and tagged v<version> after its merge (SUP.8 BP5-BP7).

validation_scenarios_dir.description: Where the validation scenarios live (VAL.1 BP1): each file naming a wish with @wish[W-<n>] is one, an automated test when it matches the stack's validation_test_files, written steps run by a person otherwise.

validation_records_dir.description: Where the validation records are stored (validation.v1), one <version>.yaml per release, added by the release pull request after the deployment to staging (VAL.1 BP3). Evidence of a baseline, not a configuration item.

slots.description: One entry per ASPICE Agent stage that a plugin fills: <plugin> or <plugin>/<skill>.

create_unit_tests_plugin.description: Stage 5, first: writes the unit tests and one stub per unit without seeing the code.

create_unit_code_plugin.description: Stage 5, second: replaces the stubs with the real units until the tests pass, never editing a test.

create_software_tests_plugin.description: Stage 8: writes the software section of the plan, the software-level tests, the measurements and the observability definitions; the coder follows.

review_pull_request_plugin.description: Stage 9: reviews the pull request from its own account with the review checklist; never the author's account.

create_validation_scenarios_plugin.description: Stage 11: writes the validation scenarios and the validation section of the plan from the wishes, the diagrams and the outside interfaces; never reads the requirements or the code.

review.description: Who reviews a pull request (SUP.1 BP1, SWE.3 BP5): a reviewer agent always; a person on every pull request that changes the architecture or the gates' own files, and on every one that is important or risky (classify_pull_request_tool).

agents.description: The host accounts the reviewer agent posts from. An approver that is none of these, no bot and not the author counts as a person.

people.description: The host accounts of the people CI calls in when a pull request needs a person's review: the checkpoint-4 review comment mentions them, so the host notifies them. Any person may approve; these are the ones asked.

config_items.description: The product's own configuration items, added to the framework's list (every path above and qf.yaml); never a way to remove one (SUP.8 BP1).

urgent_approvers.description: The host accounts that may authorize the urgent fix of a critical problem (SUP.9 BP3), with /authorize-urgent-fix on its issue before the fix merges.

change_approvers.description: The host accounts that may approve a change request (SUP.10 BP3), with /approve-change on its issue before the first commit that names it — usually the architects.

escalate_after_days.description: How many days a non-conformance may stay open before it must be escalated: labelled escalated and assigned (SUP.1 BP7).

path.description: Repository-relative, no leading slash, no parent traversal.
